PACIFIC GAS AND ELECTRIC COMPANY

ELECTRICAL UNDERGROUNDING PLAN

         ATTACHMENT C

       GLOSSARY OF TERMS




              -1175-               1
               PACIFIC GAS AND ELECTRIC COMPANY
               ELECTRICAL UNDERGROUNDING PLAN
                         ATTACHMENT C
                       GLOSSARY OF TERMS

    The purpose of this Glossary is to define key terms and acronyms used
throughout the Electrical Undergrounding Plan (EUP) and promote clarity and
consistent interpretation.
    The Glossary identifies terms with definitions from the Energy Safety EUP
Guidelines , as well as terms that PG&E has adapted for use in this EUP.
Definitions reproduced from Appendix A of the EUP Guidelines without modification
are denoted by the following symbol at the end of the definition:(ES).

                                             TERMS
Aggregate Risk Analysis
    The method for summing or aggregating risk metrics at the portfolio and system
    levels.
Alternative Mitigation
    A mitigation strategy, other than Undergrounding, used to reduce the
    consequence or likelihood of wildfires and Outage Program Events on a
    particular Circuit Segment.(ES)
Backcasting
    Recalculating prior results using updated inputs to enable consistent
    comparisons across model versions.
Backtesting
    Retrospective comparison of outputs from different risk model versions to
    assess the impact of model changes.
Baseline
    The expected risk and reliability profile of the Large Electrical Corporation’s
    existing distribution system assuming that no Undergrounding Projects from the
    EUP program are constructed during the asset life cycle. The Baseline includes
    all previously approved Undergrounding Projects, system-hardening projects,
    and similar mitigation activities.(ES)




                                        -1176-                                        2
  PG&E applies this definition to mean the “as is” system state before application
  of any EUP mitigation alternatives. This scenario incorporates EPSS and PSPS
  as operational mitigations for wildfire risk on the existing overhead system.
Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR)
    The ratio of the present value of lifetime benefits to the present value of lifetime
    costs for a mitigation. Consistent with Commission terminology, references to
    “BCR” are synonymous with the term “Cost-Benefit Ratio (CBR)” used in certain
    Commission guidance documents. See Resolution SPD-37, p. 2 n.3.
Bow Tie Model
    A standardized, PG&E Company‑wide model used to quantify enterprise risks
    in alignment with the CPUC’s Risk‑Based Decision‑Making Framework (RDF).
    Also referred to as the Enterprise Bow Tie Model.
Circuit Segment
    An isolatable circuit segment.(ES)
Committed Miles
    Undergrounding miles from scoped projects planned for completion in a
    specified year to meet annual targets.
Confirmed Project
    An Undergrounding Project that has completed Screen 3 (Project Risk
    Analysis).(ES)
Confirmed Project Polygon
    A spatial boundary generated at the beginning of Screen 3 that encompasses
    the entire Eligible Circuit Segment on which the Undergrounding Project is
    defined, except any sections already contained in another Confirmed Project
    Polygon.(ES)
Core Capabilities
    The required use-cases that the Large Electrical Corporation’s Risk Modeling
    Methodology must be able to achieve in order to make quantitative arguments
    about the risk reduction of Undergrounding and Alternative Mitigations.(ES)
Cost Efficiency
    The extent to which an activity delivers value, measured as benefits relative to
    costs.
Critical Facilities




                                         -1177-                                        3
   Facilities and infrastructure that are essential to public safety and require
   additional assistance and advance planning to ensure resiliency during Public
   Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) events.
Cumulative Risk Reduction
   Total aggregated reduction in modeled risk over a defined time horizon.
Downed Conductor Detection (DCD)
   A component of PG&E’s Enhanced Powerline Safety Settings (EPSS) that adds
   an additional protection element to address fault types not fully mitigated
   through the EPSS Program. DCD does this by enhancing the ability to quickly
   detect and de-energize low and very low initial current (high-impedance)
   line-to-ground faults before an ignition can occur.
Eligible Circuit Segment
   A Circuit Segment that falls within the risk score values that will be used to
   identify high risk Circuit Segments that are eligible for the 10-Year Electrical
   Undergrounding Program.(ES)
Enhanced Powerline Safety Settings (EPSS)
   Protective settings that reduce Ignition Risk by rapidly de-energizing lines
   experiencing faults.
Feedback Loop
   The Feedback Loop is used by PG&E for decision-support and as an evaluation
   process/tool used to analyze mitigation options for a Circuit Segment and
   generate benefit-cost and risk-reduction outcomes.
Fire Rebuild Area
   An area with four or more spans of electric distribution infrastructure damaged
   by a fire that requires the electrical distribution facilities to be reconstructed or
   repaired.
   See also Wildfire Rebuild Areas.
Fire Rebuild Projects
   Reconstruction or repair of a Circuit Segment located in a Fire Rebuild Area.
High Fire Threat District (HFTD)
   Areas of the state designated by the CPUC as having elevated wildfire risk,
   where each Electrical Corporation must take additional action to mitigate
   wildfire risk pursuant to Decision 17‑01‑009 or its successor.(ES)




                                      -1178-                                               4
High Fire Risk Area (HFRA)
   Utility-identified area considered high risk for wildfire.
High Frequency Outage Program Project-Level Standard
   The minimum decrease in Outage Program Likelihood as measured through
   formal calculations of the Key Decision‑Making Metrics that any
   Undergrounding Project considered under the High Frequency Outage Program
   must achieve to meet the required substantial increase in electrical reliability
   achieved by reducing the use of Public Safety Power Shutoffs, Enhanced
   Powerline Safety Settings, deenergization events, and any other outage
   programs.(ES)
High Frequency Outage Program Threshold
   The measure of likelihood above which is considered to have a significantly
   high likelihood of frequent or prolonged disruption of service to customers. This
   threshold must measure both likelihood of an Outage Program Event and its
   anticipated length. This threshold must represent less than 1 percent of Circuit
   Segments in the entire system by mile and no more than 10 percent of Outage
   Program Likelihood by score.(ES)
High-Risk Threshold
   The Overall Utility Risk level above which a Circuit Segment is considered
   eligible for examination for expedited undergrounding.(ES)
Hybrid Project
   A project combining undergrounding with other mitigation types on the same
   Circuit Segment.
Ignition Consequence
   The total anticipated adverse effects from a wildfire on each community it
   reaches. This metric considers wildfire hazard intensity, wildfire exposure
   potential, and the inherent wildfire vulnerabilities of communities at risk.(ES)

   PG&E applies the definition in Progress Report Table C.2 and in Chapter 7,
   Section E as follows: Ignition Consequence represents the mean expected
   damages conditional on an ignition occurring on a given circuit segment. It is
   calculated by dividing the monetized Ignition Risk by the Ignition Likelihood
   (i.e., the annual expected number of ignitions).




                                      -1179-                                          5
Ignition Likelihood
   The likelihood of an ignition at a given location given a probabilistic set of
   environmental conditions. This is an unweighted and unscaled calculation.(ES)

   PG&E applies the definition in Progress Report Table C.2 and in Chapter 7,
   Section E as follows: Ignition Likelihood, also known as the Probability of
   Ignition, is aggregated for a Circuit Segment from the suite of distribution asset
   and contact from object event probability models. The event probability models
   predict the likelihood of an ignition for an asset or location over the length of
   one fire season. Ignition Likelihood is represented in ignitions per year.
Ignition Risk
   The measure of impacts from wildfire at a given location. This metric is the
   product of two factors: (1) the likelihood a wildfire will occur, and (2) the
   potential consequences of a wildfire originating from that location.(ES) (See also
   Wildfire Risk; PG&E uses these terms interchangeably).

   PG&E applies the definition in Progress Report Table C.2 and in Chapter 7,
   Section E as follows: Ignition risks are Circuit Segment relative risk values
   based on the outputs of the WDRM. Ignition Risk is the product of the
   Probability of Ignition for an asset or location and the Wildfire Consequence at
   that location. The relative WDRM risk values are then calibrated against the
   absolute value of PG&E’s Enterprise Risk Bow Tie for distribution Wildfire Risk.
   Ignition Risk is represented as a dollar value.
Ignition Tail Risk Threshold
   The measure of consequence above which a Circuit Segment is considered to
   have significant potential for catastrophic wildfire, such that it merits special
   consideration. This threshold must represent less than 1 percent of Circuit
   Segments in the entire system by mile and no more than 10 percent of the
   wildfire consequence by score.(ES)
Ignition-Weighted Consequence
   A consequence metric weighted by Ignition Likelihood to emphasize higher-risk
   locations.




                                      -1180-                                            6
In-Area Circuit Segment
   A Circuit Segment located within the Large Electrical Corporation’s service
   territory that is located in a Tier 2 or 3 High Fire‑Threat District or a Wildfire
   Rebuild Area.(ES)
Ineligible Circuit Segment
   A Circuit Segment that does not meet any Project-Level Thresholds and is
   removed from further evaluation.
Instantaneous Risk Reduction
   The reduction in modeled risk at a specific point in time relative to baseline.
Interruption Cost Estimate (ICE) Calculator
   A customer survey–based model developed by Lawrence Berkeley National
   Laboratory (LBNL) that estimates the economic impacts of power outages on
   customers based on outage duration, timing, and customer characteristics.
JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Data Submissions
   A data file type designed to track unstructured data that would not be
   appropriate for a spreadsheet format.(ES)
Key Decision-Making Metrics (KDMMs)
   The key decision‑making metrics developed pursuant to Section 2.7.3 of the
   EUP Guidelines.(ES)
Line Elimination Incentive Program (LEIP)
   LEIP is a system hardening and wildfire risk reduction program through which
   PG&E provides financial incentives to property owners who voluntarily agree to
   permanently discontinue electric service, enabling the removal of overhead
   distribution facilities in High Fire Threat Districts and High Fire Risk Areas.
Line Removal Program
   A PG&E system hardening program that eliminates overhead lines using
   remote grids, incentives, and land acquisition.
Mitigated Circuit Segment Standards
   The Project‑Level risk scores that an Eligible Circuit Segment must reach to be
   considered sufficiently mitigated under the terms of the EUP. These standards
   consist of the High‑Risk Project‑Level Standard, the Ignition Tail Risk
   Project‑Level Standard, and the High Frequency Outage Program Project‑Level
   Standard.(ES)




                                      -1181-                                            7
Model Risk Landscape (MRL)
   The model risk landscape defined for the EUP pursuant to Section 2.7.4 of the
   EUP Guidelines.(ES)
Non-Cumulative
   A metric that can only be expressed at a single point in time.
Non-EUP Project
   A distribution undergrounding or other system‑hardening project in Tier 2 or 3
   High Fire‑Threat District that is funded or in the Project Planning and
   Construction Phases that is not included in the 10‑Year EUP.(ES)
Non-Ratepayer Funding
   External funding sources used to offset Project costs.
Non-Undergrounding Subproject
   A Subproject that uses an alternative system hardening mitigation other than
   undergrounding. Any resulting risk reduction is not counted toward EUP
   objectives.
Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Costs
   Expected lifetime costs to operate and maintain electric utility distribution
   assets.
Outage Program
   An Outage Program is: (i) any program that interrupts electrical service for the
   purpose of mitigating or avoiding the risk of causing a wildfire including Public
   Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) programs, fast trip settings (including enhanced
   powerline safety settings, Fast Curve Settings, and Sensitive Relay Profile) and
   similar programs, and (ii) any program that could result in a deenergization
   event. Outage Programs exclude maintenance outages and other outages not
   related to reducing wildfire risk.(ES)
Outage Program Consequence
   The total anticipated adverse effects from an Outage Program for a community.
   This considers the Outage Program exposure potential and inherent Outage
   Program vulnerabilities of communities at risk.(ES)

   PG&E applies the definition in Progress Report Table C.2 and in Chapter 7,
   Section E as follows: The quantified the impact of an outage caused by an
   Outage Program on a Circuit Segment in dollars per outage minute and is used



                                       -1182-                                          8
   to estimate the customer impact in terms of the Value of Service (VoS) lost for
   the count and type of customers impacted.
Outage Program Likelihood
   The likelihood of a Large Electrical Corporation utilizing an Outage Program
   given a probabilistic set of environmental conditions.(ES)

   PG&E applies the definition in Progress Report Table C.2 and in Chapter 7,
   Section E as follows: The expected number of outage minutes per year caused
   by an Outage Program on a Circuit Segment. It is calculated by summing the
   EPSS Likelihood and PSPS Likelihood.
Outage Program Risk
   The measure of reliability impacts from Outage Programs at a given location.
   This metric is the product of two factors: (1) the likelihood an Outage Program
   Event will be required due to environmental conditions exceeding design
   conditions; and (2) the potential consequences of the Outage Program for
   affected customers, considering exposure potential and vulnerability. This is an
   unweighted and unscaled calculation.(ES)

   PG&E applies the definition in Progress Report Table C.2 and in Chapter 7,
   Section E as follows: The summation of EPSS Risk and PSPS Risk,
   representing the total monetized impact of outages caused by an Outage
   Program and is used to calculate the Overall Utility Risk.
Outage Program Risk Model (OPRM)
   The model used to estimate reliability risk from Outage Programs such as
   PSPS and EPSS.
Overall Utility Risk (OUR)
   The combined measure of Ignition Risk and Outage Program Risk that
   measures the total risk of wildfires and Outage Program Events related to
   wildfire risks. This is computed as the inner product of the likelihoods of
   adverse events and their consequences. This is an unweighted and unscaled
   calculation.(ES)

   PG&E applies the definition in Progress Report Table C.2 and in Chapter 7,
   Section E as follows: Overall Utility Risk is the combination of Ignition Risk and
   Outage Program Risk, along with considerations for climate change and



                                     -1183-                                             9
   escalation. This is represented as a dollar value and is an unscaled and
   unweighted value.
Overhead System Hardening
   Upgrades to overhead infrastructure to reduce wildfire and reliability risk,
   including installing stronger, more resistant poles and replacing bare powerlines
   with covered conductor.
Plan Mitigation Objective (PMO)
   The amount of change in risk (wildfire and reliability) that is necessary to meet
   the substantiality requirements of section 8388.5(d)(2).(ES)

   PG&E uses the term PMO as the amount of Overall Utility Risk targeted to be
   reduced for each primary overhead mile removed, applied across the EUP
   portfolio to drive consistent performance as the EUP progresses.
Plan Tracking Objectives (PTO)
   Forward‑looking, quantifiable measurements and objectives, measured at the
   Portfolio‑Level and System‑Level, used to assess progress toward the Plan
   Mitigation Objective.(ES)
Plant Maintenance (PM) Order
   A unique identifier representing a work order in PG&E’s internal tracking system
   used to plan, execute, track, and close maintenance or construction work on
   utility assets.
Portfolio
   The set of all Confirmed Projects at Screen 3 or later. A portfolio is a unique list
   of Confirmed Projects, and adding or removing Confirmed Projects from the list
   constitutes an update to the Portfolio and must be indicated with a new portfolio
   ID.(ES)
Portfolio-Level
   A measurement that accumulates information from every Circuit Segment on
   each Circuit which has one or more Confirmed Projects as well as the effects of
   Confirmed Projects on the overall Circuit into a single number.(ES)
Portfolio-Level Metrics
   Metrics aggregating impacts across multiple projects or Circuit Segments.
Portfolio-Level Risk Reduction
   Total reduction in risk achieved across the EUP portfolio.
Portfolio-Level Standards

                                     -1184-                                         10
   The Ignition Risk Decrease Standard and the Reliability Increase Standard.(ES)
Primary Overhead Mile Removed
   A unit representing one mile of overhead line removed and placed
   underground.
Prioritized Project
   An Undergrounding Project that has passed Screen 4 (Prioritization and
   Finalization).(ES)
Project
   A Circuit Segment with planned or in progress Wildfire System Hardening work.
Project Acceptance Framework
   The multi‑step process, described in Section 2.4 of the EUP Guidelines, that the
   Large Electrical Corporation will use to create the list of Undergrounding
   Projects pursuant to Section 8388.5(c)(2), to select Undergrounding Projects for
   construction, and to maintain and update the Circuit Segment Information Lists
   throughout the EUP 10‑year period.(ES)
Project as Scoped
   The full evaluated project scope, including all mitigation components.
Project Management Template
   A standardized tool for tracking project schedule, milestones, and progress.
Project-Level
   A measurement that accumulates risk from all of the equipment on a single
   Circuit Segment into a single number.(ES)
Project-Level Standards
   The High‑Risk Project‑Level Standard, the High Frequency Outage Program
   Project‑Level Standard, and the Tail Risk Project‑Level Standard.(ES)
Project-Level Thresholds
   The High‑Risk Threshold, Ignition Tail Risk Threshold, and High Frequency
   Outage Program Threshold.(ES)
Pro-Rata Risk Allocation
   Allocation of risk proportional to segment length.
Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS)
   A PG&E Outage Program that proactively de-energizes powerlines during high
   wildfire risk conditions.




                                    -1185-                                        11
Reliability Risk
    Risk associated with power outages and service interruptions.
Remote Grid
    A standalone energy system used to replace overhead lines and enable line
    removal.
Reserve Miles
    Additional planned Undergrounding Project miles that can be advanced if
    necessary.
Risk Density
    Risk density represents the concentration of risk within a given unit of
    infrastructure, typically expressed as risk per mile. While total risk reflects
    overall exposure, risk density helps identify where mitigation investments can
    achieve the greatest risk reduction per mile treated. PG&E uses risk density to
    target system hardening resources to the portions of the system where they can
    most effectively reduce risk.
Risk Model Change Factor for Ignition Risk
    An adjustment input to the Risk Model Impact Factor that represents the
    observed variance across Ignition Risk models (e.g., WDRM v3 (previous
    version of the wildfire risk model) vs. WDRM v4 (current version of the wildfire
    risk model).
Risk Model Change Factor for Outage Risk
    An adjustment input to the Risk Model Impact Factor that represents the
    observed variance in Outage Risk models (e.g., Interruption Cost Estimate
    (ICE) 1.0 vs. ICE 2.0 value of service).
Risk Model Impact Factor
    An adjustment factor, derived from the Risk Model Change Factors for Ignition
    Risk and Outage Risk, that quantifies the overall impact of risk model updates
    on Overall Utility Risk. The Risk Model Impact Factor is applied to key
    performance metrics, including the Plan Mitigation Objective and Plan Tracking
    Objective, to account for changes in modeled risk resulting from updates to the
    Ignition Risk and Outage Program Risk Models. This adjustment helps
    maintain the consistency and comparability of risk reduction metrics and
    performance results over time.




                                      -1186-                                          12
Risk Reduced per Mile Installed
   Monetized risk reduction achieved per mile of mitigation installed.
Risk Reduced per Mile of Overhead Removed
   Monetized risk reduction achieved per mile of primary overhead electric
   facilities removed.
Risk Reporting Unit (RRU)
   A standardized unit used for reporting modeled risk.

   Defined in CPUC Resolution SPD-37 as: A CPUC-jurisdictional effort within
   Electric Operations or Gas Operations that simultaneously removes or mitigates
   the risk associated with a group of contiguous assets or systems that exhibit
   high levels of risk. The RRU must include common elements that must include,
   but are not limited to Consequence Attributes, Risk level, line-item costs,
   benefit-cost ratios (CBRs), work units, and time. The RRU can be aggregated
   along several dimensions based on unique identifiers that include, but are not
   limited to, hierarchy, scenario, version, risk event, tranche, and mitigation types.
Short Circuit Segment
   Circuit Segments that are less than one mile in length.
Subproject
   A delimited portion of work on a Confirmed Project. A Subproject must have a
   uniform set of mitigations applied to the entire Subproject. If a project does not
   have a uniform set of mitigations, it must be divided into more Subprojects.(ES)
System-Level
   A measurement that accumulates information from the entire electrical
   distribution system into a single number.(ES)
Undergrounding Program
   PG&E’s program to relocate overhead lines underground to reduce Wildfire
   Risk and Outage Program Risk.
Undergrounding Project
   An Eligible Circuit Segment that has completed Screen 2, including the CPUC
   Data Appendix 1 information completed.(ES)
Undergrounding Subproject
   A Subproject that is comprised of only Undergrounding activities, including the
   Undergrounding Support Work necessary to complete the Undergrounding
   Subproject.(ES)

                                     -1187-                                         13
Wildfire Benefit Cost Analysis (WBCA)
   A PG&E model used to evaluate costs and benefits of mitigation options over
   asset life.
Wildfire Distribution Risk Model (WDRM)
   The PG&E model used to estimate wildfire risk at the Circuit Segment level.
Wildfire Rebuild Area
   A location where distribution infrastructure has been damaged by wildfire that is
   specifically identified by the Large Electrical Corporation in the EUP or in a
   Progress Report.(ES)

   PG&E uses the term ‘Fire Rebuild Area’ to refer to areas with four or more
   spans of electric distribution infrastructure damaged by a fire that requires the
   electrical distribution facilities to be reconstructed or repaired.
Wildfire Risk
   The measure of impacts from wildfire at a given location. This metric is the
   product of two factors: (1) the likelihood a wildfire will occur, and (2) the
   potential consequences of a wildfire originating from that location. (See also
   Ignition Risk; PG&E uses these terms interchangeably).
Workplan/EUP Workplan
   The set of Projects and Subprojects planned for completion under the EUP.
